title: Prophecies of Christ
tagline: Hard mode: from the prophets’ promises to the Gospels’ fulfillment.
description: Old Testament prophecies paired with their New Testament fulfillment, drawn from the NIV. Hard mode: know your prophets, psalms and chapter-and-verse.

questions.q: Which prophet foretold that a ruler over Israel would come from little Bethlehem?
questions.reveal: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem as the ruler’s hometown — and in Matthew 2, Herod’s scholars quote it to point the way to the newborn King.

questions.q: In Matthew 2, when Herod asks where the Messiah will be born, who answers by quoting Micah?
choices: Chief priests and teachers of the law
questions.reveal: Herod gathered the chief priests and teachers of the law. They answered “In Bethlehem in Judea” and cited Micah 5:2. It was the Magi who then made the trip.

questions.q: Isaiah foretold a virgin’s son called Immanuel. What does Matthew say “Immanuel” means?
questions.reveal: Matthew 1:22–23 quotes Isaiah 7:14 and explains the name: Immanuel means “God with us.” That’s the heart of Christmas in two words.

questions.q: Gabriel told Mary her son would reign on David’s throne forever, echoing God’s promise to David through which prophet?
questions.reveal: In 2 Samuel 7, God spoke through Nathan to promise David an offspring whose throne and kingdom would endure forever. Gabriel’s words to Mary in Luke 1:32–33 echo that promise.

questions.q: Matthew says the Holy Family’s return from Egypt fulfilled “Out of Egypt I called my son.” Which prophet wrote it?
questions.reveal: Hosea 11:1 recalls God calling Israel out of Egypt. Matthew 2:15 sees Jesus, God’s true Son, retracing Israel’s story.

questions.q: Matthew links Herod’s killing of Bethlehem’s boys to Rachel weeping for her children. In what town is her voice heard?
questions.reveal: Jeremiah 31:15: “A voice is heard in Ramah… Rachel weeping for her children” (NIV). Matthew 2:17–18 quotes it over the grief Herod caused.

questions.q: Isaiah foresaw a voice in the wilderness preparing the way for the Lord. Whom do the Gospels identify as that voice?
questions.reveal: Matthew 3:3 applies Isaiah 40:3 to John the Baptist, and in John 1:23 John uses the words to describe himself.

questions.q: Mark 1:2–3 says “as it is written in Isaiah,” but its first line, about God sending a messenger, comes from which book?
questions.reveal: Mark blends Malachi 3:1 (“I will send my messenger”) with Isaiah 40:3 under Isaiah’s name. Jesus applies Malachi 3:1 to John the Baptist in Matthew 11:10.

questions.q: Malachi promised God would send which prophet before the great day of the Lord, someone Jesus said came in John the Baptist?
questions.reveal: Malachi 4:5 promises Elijah’s return. Jesus said of John, “he is the Elijah who was to come” (Matthew 11:14, NIV), and Luke 1:17 says John came in Elijah’s spirit and power.

questions.q: When Jesus settled in Capernaum, Matthew quoted Isaiah’s promise of light dawning on which two tribal lands?
questions.reveal: Isaiah 9:1–2 promises that the people of Zebulun and Naphtali, who walked in darkness, would see a great light. Matthew 4:13–16 says it dawned when Jesus made his home in Capernaum.

questions.q: In which town’s synagogue did Jesus read Isaiah 61 and announce, “Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing”?
questions.reveal: In Luke 4:16–21, back in Nazareth where he grew up, Jesus read Isaiah 61:1–2: good news for the poor, freedom for prisoners, sight for the blind. Then he said it was fulfilled that day.

questions.q: Matthew 8:17 cites Isaiah 53:4, “He took up our infirmities,” right after Jesus does what?
questions.reveal: One evening at Capernaum, Jesus drove out spirits and healed all the sick who were brought to him. Matthew 8:16–17 says this fulfilled Isaiah 53:4.

questions.q: Matthew 12 quotes Isaiah 42: God’s servant won’t break a bruised reed or snuff out what?
questions.reveal: Isaiah 42:3 pictures a Servant so gentle he won’t snuff out a smoldering wick. Matthew 12:17–21 applies the whole passage to Jesus’ quiet, compassionate ministry.

questions.q: Jesus said no sign would be given except the sign of which prophet, who spent three days and nights in a huge fish?
questions.reveal: Jonah 1:17 records three days and three nights in the fish. In Matthew 12:39–40, Jesus himself draws the parallel: the Son of Man will spend three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

questions.q: Matthew 13:35’s “I will open my mouth in parables” quotes Psalm 78. Whose name appears in that psalm’s title?
questions.reveal: Psalm 78 is titled “A maskil of Asaph.” Matthew says the words were spoken “through the prophet” and sees them fulfilled as Jesus taught the crowds in parables.

questions.q: Jesus told Nicodemus the Son of Man must be lifted up just as Moses lifted up what in the wilderness?
questions.reveal: In Numbers 21:8–9, anyone bitten who looked at the bronze snake on its pole lived. In John 3:14–15, Jesus himself makes the comparison: whoever believes in the lifted-up Son of Man has eternal life.

questions.q: In Acts 3:22, Peter quotes the promise of “a prophet like me” and applies it to Jesus. Who first said it?
questions.reveal: In Deuteronomy 18:15, Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like him from among the people. Peter tells the crowd at the temple that Jesus is that Prophet.

questions.q: Zechariah told Daughter Zion that her king would come lowly and riding on what?
questions.reveal: Zechariah 9:9 describes a humble king on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey. Matthew 21:4–5 and John 12:14–15 quote it as Jesus rides into Jerusalem.

questions.q: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” Jesus quotes this line from which psalm?
questions.reveal: Jesus quotes Psalm 118:22 to the temple leaders in Matthew 21:42. Peter later uses the same verse before the Sanhedrin in Acts 4:11.

questions.q: Jesus asked the Pharisees how the Messiah could be David’s son if David calls him “Lord.” Which psalm did he quote?
questions.reveal: Psalm 110:1: “The LORD says to my lord: ‘Sit at my right hand’” (NIV). In Matthew 22:41–46, no one could answer Jesus. Peter quotes the same verse at Pentecost (Acts 2:34–35).

questions.q: In John 13:18 Jesus applies Psalm 41:9 to his betrayer, a trusted friend who had shared what with him?
questions.reveal: Psalm 41:9 grieves a close friend who shared my bread and then turned against me. At the Last Supper, Jesus says the verse is being fulfilled, and Judas soon leaves.

questions.q: After the Last Supper, Jesus quoted “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.” Which prophet?
questions.reveal: Jesus quotes Zechariah 13:7 in Matthew 26:31, warning that all the disciples would fall away that night. They scattered at his arrest (Matthew 26:56).

questions.q: At the Last Supper, Jesus said a line from Isaiah 53 “must be fulfilled in me.” Which line?
choices: Led like a lamb to the slaughter
questions.reveal: In Luke 22:37, Jesus quotes Isaiah 53:12, “And he was numbered with the transgressors” (NIV). Hours later he was crucified between two criminals.

questions.q: Matthew 27:9 says the thirty silver coins and potter’s field fulfilled words of a prophet. Which prophet does Matthew name?
questions.reveal: Matthew names Jeremiah, though the wording most closely matches Zechariah 11:12–13 (thirty silver thrown to the potter). Many see it blended with Jeremiah’s field purchase (Jer 32) and potter (Jer 18–19).

questions.q: Under oath before Caiaphas, Jesus echoed Daniel 7: the Son of Man coming on what?
questions.reveal: Daniel 7:13 sees “one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven” (NIV). When Jesus claimed those words in Matthew 26:64, the high priest tore his clothes and charged blasphemy.

questions.q: Psalm 22:18 foretold what would happen to the sufferer’s clothing. What did the soldiers at the cross do?
questions.reveal: The soldiers divided Jesus’ clothes and cast lots for his seamless undergarment. John 19:23–24 says this fulfilled Psalm 22:18.

questions.q: From the cross Jesus cried, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” These words open which psalm?
questions.reveal: Jesus prayed the first line of Psalm 22, which moves from anguish to praise and describes mocking, thirst and divided clothes. See Matthew 27:46.

questions.q: After a soldier’s spear, John 19:37 quotes “They will look on the one they have pierced.” Which prophet wrote it?
questions.reveal: Zechariah 12:10 foresees Jerusalem looking on “the one they have pierced” (NIV) and mourning. John cites it right after the soldier pierced Jesus’ side.

questions.q: At Pentecost, Peter said Psalm 16’s holy one who would not see decay couldn’t be David himself. Why not?
choices: David was taken up like Elijah
questions.reveal: Peter noted that David died and was buried, and his tomb was still there. So Psalm 16:10 foretold the Messiah, whom God raised before his body saw decay (Acts 2:27–31).

questions.q: Philip met a traveler in a chariot reading Isaiah 53, “led like a sheep to the slaughter.” Who was he?
questions.reveal: In Acts 8, Philip started from Isaiah 53:7–8 and told the Ethiopian treasury official the good news about Jesus. The man was baptized that same day.
